surprises.description: Millrose authorized a $250 million buyback and said it will direct 10% of earnings to repurchases when shares are below book value, while distributing 90% of earnings. The preview identified a buyback as a key test and included authorization in its bull case, but did not present it as the expected outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized a new $250 million share repurchase program,” with a policy to “distribute 90% of earnings and direct 10% toward buybacks while shares trade below book value of $35.24 per share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview called the buyback question “the cleanest test of whether management believes its own book value” and listed “buyback authorized” in its bull scenario.

surprises.description: The rental pilot is larger than the preview’s cited estimate: Millrose reported 1,233 homes costing about $333 million, versus the preview’s account of roughly 1,096 homes for about $290 million. At the same time, Millrose said the purchases represent just over 1% of its asset base, with about $50 million more in future build-to-rent commitments.
surprises.fact_evidence: The pilot involved “purchasing 1,233 completed homes across 18 states for ~$333 million,” a “net ~$120 million investment,” representing “just over 1%” of the asset base, plus “~$50 million of future build-to-rent commitments.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described allegations that Millrose bought “~1,096 finished homes from Lennar (~$290M, 16 states)” and flagged a bear case of a BTR book “larger than $290M and still growing with no cap.”

surprises.description: The disclosed rental economics were mixed against the preview’s concern about returns below financing costs: the pilot was underwritten at a 5% going-in cap rate, but early rents are pacing about 10% above underwriting. Only roughly 10% of the homes had been leased so far, and the facts do not provide the net yield after operating costs that the preview requested.
surprises.fact_evidence: The pilot was underwritten at a “~5% going-in cap rate” and “~8% unlevered IRR (10–12% levered),” with “early rents pacing ~10% above underwriting” and “roughly 10% of homes leased so far.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview highlighted a concern that rental returns could be below debt costs, citing estimated rent after taxes and insurance of “~5.92%” against note coupons of “6.50%/6.75%,” and called for disclosure of net yield after expenses.

surprises.description: Pro forma for Dream Finders, 42% of Millrose’s asset base is outside Lennar, a larger non-Lennar share than the preview’s cited 32% of invested capital in other agreements. This indicates more diversification than that prior portfolio mix suggested, although the measures are not identical.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pro forma for the Dream Finders transaction, approximately 42% of Millrose's asset base is now invested outside the Lennar Master Program Agreement.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said Lennar was “68% of invested capital” and the “other agreements” book was 32%.

surprises.description: Q4 AFFO guidance rose to $0.82–$0.84 per share, and management expects the year-end run rate to exceed the prior $3.30 guidance. That is above the preview’s roughly $0.80 Q2 exit run rate, but the quarterly range does not exceed the preview’s stated buy-side hurdle of more than $0.84.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management “raised Q4 AFFO guidance to approximately $0.82–$0.84 per share” and expects “a year-end run rate above the prior $3.30 per share guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the Q2 exit run rate was “~$0.80” and that the buy-side needed “>$0.84” to believe the Dream Finders/Beazer commitment was accretive.

surprises.description: Net takedown proceeds were $800 million, down from the preview’s cited Q2 level of $1.0 billion, but not as low as the preview’s warning threshold of around $700 million or below. The sequential decline is a negative, while the proceeds remained above the level identified as a sharper concern.
surprises.fact_evidence: During Q3 Millrose “received ~$800 million in net takedown proceeds.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited Q2 net cash proceeds of “$1.0B” and said “a drop toward $700M or below” would reframe the company as balance-sheet-constrained.

surprises.description: Non-Lennar yields rose to 10.8%, modestly above the preview’s cited 10.6% yield on the other-agreements book. Management also expects that yield to reach about 11% in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: Millrose said non-Lennar yields were “rising to 10.8% and expected to reach ~11% in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “10.6% on the 19-counterparty ‘other agreements’ book.”
